title: The Language Interpretability Tool: Extensible, Interactive Visualizations and Analysis for NLP Models
abstract: Ian Tenney, James Wexler, Jasmijn Bastings, Tolga Bolukbasi, Andy Coenen, Sebastian Gehrmann, Ellen Jiang, Mahima Pushkarna, Carey Radebaugh, Emily Reif, Ann Yuan. Proceedings of the 2020 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: System Demonstrations. 2020.
core_contribution: Introduces the Language Interpretability Tool (LIT), an open-source platform for visualization and understanding of NLP models, integrating local explanations, aggregate analysis, and counterfactual generation into a streamlined, browser-based interface.
conclusion: LIT provides an integrated UI and a suite of components for visualizing and exploring the behavior of NLP models, enabling interactive analysis at the single-datapoint level and over a whole dataset, with first-class support for counterfactual generation and evaluation.
limitation: LIT is an evaluation tool and not directly useful for training-time monitoring.
LIT does not scale to large datasets as well as offline tools (handles about 10,000 examples at once).
LIT is framework-agnostic and does not have deep model integration like some other tools.
future_direction: Additional metrics and visualizations for sequence and structured output types
Greater ability to customize the UI for different applications
